claims.title: Delft 2015 CHSH statistic recomputed from the released data
claims.scope: the 4746 released heralding attempts of the Delft 2015 loophole-free Bell test and the authors' published valid-trial filter
assumptions: the 4TU archive matches md5 342f29f8288c46575818acd2acebd535 and the committed sha256
the valid-trial filter and readout windows are those of the authors' published analysis script
the local-model win bound is 3/4 + 3(tau + tau^2) with the paper's setting-predictability bound tau = 1.08e-5
nonclaims: the check reproduces n = 245, k = 196, S = 2.42 +- 0.20 and p = 0.039; it does not re-derive the filter from detector physics
the check does not assess the experiment's loophole analysis beyond the published bound
a Bell violation is not evidence for or against a simulation hypothesis

claims.title: Delft correlations on the canonical CHSH disk
claims.scope: the equal-weight least-squares visibility-phase point of the four recomputed Delft correlations
assumptions: the Delft schedule equals the canonical CHSH schedule with every setting difference shifted by pi
the correlations are read through the repository's singlet law E = -v cos(theta - phi)
nonclaims: the fitted point q = (0.856, -0.094) is a least-squares summary, not a maximum-likelihood state estimate
local models need not lie in the visibility-phase family; only the coordinate x = S / (2 sqrt 2) is compared with the chord

claims.title: NIST beacon bits keep the composite simulation Bayes factor below the Ville threshold
claims.scope: 131072 bits from NIST Randomness Beacon 2.0 chain 2 pulses 1987000 to 1987255, with pulse 1987256 used only for verification
assumptions: the committed localRandomValue fields pass all 256 SHA-512 precommitment links
the test is the Krichevsky-Trofimov composite Bayes factor against fair IID bits
nonclaims: NIST signatures and output-value hashes are not verified
passing one composite test is not a randomness certification
fair-looking bits do not show that the world is or is not simulated

claims.title: (standard) Composite Bayes-factor detection rate: expectation of the Krichevsky-Trofimov regret bound
claims.scope: IID bits, a fair base law, and a restricted simulation hypothesis with unknown bias under a Beta(1/2,1/2) prior
assumptions: observations are IID Bernoulli under each hypothesis
the simulation hypothesis is restricted to a Bernoulli signature declared in advance
nonclaims: the pathwise regret bound is Krichevsky-Trofimov 1981 (see also Willems-Shtarkov-Tjalkens 1995); not claimed as new; only taking its expectation under a biased Bernoulli source is recorded here, and a self-contained proof is in ST-T272
the bound E[log BF_n] >= n KL(q || 1/2) - (1/2) ln n - ln 2 says nothing about simulators that reproduce the fair law exactly
the theorem does not cover dependent, adaptive, or adversarially chosen bit sources

claims.title: Binary symmetric coarsening slows restricted-signature detection
claims.scope: a Bernoulli(q) simulated source observed through one binary symmetric channel with flip probability f in [0, 1/2]
assumptions: the channel acts independently on every bit and is known to the observer
nonclaims: the result concerns one declared channel and does not bound arbitrary observation coarsenings
slower detection is not evidence that a source is unsimulated
